findings: B21 Lemma 2.3's proof (BTZ_1.tex:654) asserts that the gluing M2 is a E_{>=0}-manifold without proving it Hausdorff; it is, for the normalisation chosen here (CylChartData.t2Space_glued: the graph of κ⁻¹ on the overlap is closed because the overlap lies in the compact {v−ε/2 ≤ τ ≤ v+ε/2, r ≤ ε/4} inside the chart cylinder — points of 𝒫 ∩ cyl above Π are in J⁺(κ⁻¹Π), CylChartData.mem_glueF). For a careless choice of the glued piece (e.g. the full closed spear S, as printed, or a piece leaving the chart domain below Π) Hausdorffness can fail; B21 should say which neighbourhood of S is glued. l.666–667 uses CBG universality where it says 'Cauchy-maximal' (IsE0CauchyMaximal.exists_morphism_of_dev).

B21 Lemma 2.3's proof does not argue that M2 is globally hyperbolic: it proves Σ Cauchy in M2 and concludes 'M0 → M2 is a Cauchy-embedding', which in B21's own Def (Cauchy embedding between globally hyperbolic spacetimes) needs GH of M2 first, or a 'Cauchy surface ⇒ GH' theorem for E_{>=0}-manifolds that the paper uses tacitly.

B21 Lemma 2.3's proof (l.642) uses 'a time function whose level sets are C¹ submanifolds' (Bernard–Surh); only a Cauchy surface strictly below the disc Π is needed (CylChartData.exists_cauchy_subset_W0 uses a level of a continuous Cauchy time function, any level below min T on κ⁻¹Π), as SCOPE K-2 noted. B21 also leaves M0's connectedness implicit.

B21 Def 2.1 (l.611–620): with φ(p) = (−2R,0,0) and f = τ − r/2, the head is {f = −2R, r ≤ R} = {r = 2(τ + 2R)}, meeting r = R at τ = −3R/2, and the shaft is {r = R, τ ≥ −3R/2}; the printed {r = 2(τ − R)} and {τ ≥ 0} fit neither this vertex nor each other (the normalisation of Lemma 2.4's proof, Φ(p) = (−R/2,0,0), makes the shaft start at τ = 0). Proved in the corrected form: frontier_spear. U = ψ(spear) is closed, not open — PROVED in M for M globally hyperbolic (isClosed_spearImage; the hypothesis of Lemmas 2.3/2.4): its interior is ψ({f > v, r < R}) (interior_spearImage) and its boundary in M is ψ(head ∪ shaft) (frontier_spearImage, IsSpearNbhd.frontier_eq); 'neighbourhood of ]p,+∞[' holds (IsSpearNbhd.exists_ray_mem_nhds for the chart ray; IsSpearNbhd.mem_nhds_of_line for ]p,+∞[ ⊆ Δ itself, via IsFullFutureBTZRay.exists_eq_of_line). (Before fixer round 1 the closedness was asserted here without proof; WP-44d/WP-46b audits.)

B21 Lemma 2.3's proof (BTZ_1.tex:647) shrinks the chart neighbourhood so that Π is acausal in M, and l.661 ('the boundary of M₀ in M₂ is Π') needs it: without it a causal curve leaving the cylinder from κ⁻¹Π and returning below Π removes points from M₀ that stay as extra points of the spear piece. Formalized: the normalisation holds in the stronger form 'chart cylinder causally convex in M' (CylChartData.convex, proved from strong causality in exists_cylChartData), which gives acausality of κ⁻¹Π (isAcausal_K) and the overlap 𝒫 ∩ cyl ∩ {τ < v+ε/2} (mem_U10_iff). The paper's argument is correct here; round 1's formalization had omitted the normalisation (audit round 2 major), now repaired.

B21 Lemma 2.3's proof (BTZ_1.tex:642–670) needs M₀ = M ∖ J⁺(φ⁻¹Π) connected (CBG developments are connected) and leaves it implicit; it is true for every connected GH E₀-manifold, through the connectedness of a (non-compact) closed Cauchy surface (WP-43a: isConnected_of_isCauchySurface_closed, with R1 = sfa_isCompact_Jplus_inter_Jminus replacing compactness).

DEC-108, B21 Lemma 2.3 (BTZ_1.tex:660–667): the global hyperbolicity of M2 = M0 ∪ 𝒫, never argued in B21, is TRUE and proved directly: M2 is a Causal.Causality.TwoPiece (absolutely minimal charted causality, overlap 𝒫 ∩ {τ < v+ε/2} causally convex in both pieces, relations agreeing) so it is causal and its unmixed diamonds are diamonds of a GH piece; the mixed diamonds J(x,y), x ∈ M0, y ∈ 𝒫 above Π, where M0 and 𝒫 have no common Cauchy surface (so TwoPiece.isCompact_diamond_mixed does not apply), are j(D0) ∪ Ψ(D1) with D1 = {τ ≥ v+ε/2} ∩ J⁻(y) ∩ J⁺(G) compact in 𝔼₀, D0 = J⁺_M(x) ∩ J⁻_M(κ⁻¹H) compact in M (H the points of the disc level below y, G those above x), j the continuous map M0 ∪ κ⁻¹(𝒫 ∩ cyl) → M2 (CylChartData.isCompact_diamond_mixed). The converse inclusion needs that a relation of M from M0 to a point κ⁻¹w of κ⁻¹Π passes through the overlap (exists_overlap_of_le, a connectedness argument on a causal curve), which B21 does not state.

B21 Lemma 2.3's c = c0 ∪ c1 argument (l.660–666): the step 'c1 reaches Π' is the fact that no inextensible causal curve of M2 stays in 𝒫 above Π; proved (CylChartData.not_inextensible_above): read in paper coordinates its past end has τ, r monotone and bounded (τ ≥ v+ε/2), converges in 𝔼₀ (E0.exists_tendsto_of_bddBelow) to a point still in 𝒫, and is adjoined there (pastExtensible_gluePaper). Uniqueness of the intersection needs the causality of M2 (TwoPiece.isCausal) and the acausality of Σ in M; both supplied.

findings: B21 Lemma 2.4's proof, l.725: 'if q is in the future of q' should read 'of p'.

B21 Lemma 2.4's proof (l.727–741): the existence of the graph over D_R comes from transversality of the SMOOTH spacelike Σ at w = Σ ∩ Δ followed by shrinking R; the broken curves c_{θ0,r0} give 'at most once'. The paper's argument is complete in its smooth setting. For a topological Cauchy surface (this file) transversality is unavailable and existence over the whole disc is obtained instead from inextensibility of the vertical null rays of the spear chart (spear_vertical_noLimit, via axis_noLimit and B21 prop:isom_strong) and connectedness (spear_vertical_meets). (Round 0's finding said the paper's argument was incomplete; that was a misreading and is withdrawn.)

DEC-108, B21 Lemma 2.4's case 'q in the future of p' (l.725–733): TRUE and proved. B21 'chooses the φ_i and φ so that the changes of charts are the identity' and glues; two steps are left implicit and are where the work is: (i) a change of chart is a restriction of an isometry of 𝔼₀ only on a CONNECTED overlap (on another component of the overlap a different isometry may act), so the normalisation is made on the component U0 of the vertex (btzE0_localUnique_core + rigidity e0_eqOn_of_eqOn_open); (ii) the glued Φ must be injective, which B21 does not argue: here Φ = ψ on W1 ∪ U0 (W1 the spear above the level w+η/3) and κ⁻¹ ∘ e on U0 ∪ L (L below that level), and a point of the spear sent by ψ into the chart cylinder lies in U0 because the whole causal diamond from the vertex is sent into the (causally convex) cylinder. The finite cover of [p,q] is replaced by a continuation (infimum of the good parameters), one chart cylinder at a time.

B21 Lemma 2.4 (BTZ_1.tex:690) is false as written for B21's Cauchy surfaces, which are topological hypersurfaces (l.224): 'graph of a smooth positive function' fails. Counterexample (paper level, not formalized): M = 𝔼₀ (GH, the identity is a spear chart of every axis point), Σ = {τ = |Re z|/4}. Along a future causal curve |dz| ≤ 2dτ (the E₀ metric −2dτdr + dr² + r²dθ²), so T = τ − |Re z|/4 increases at rate ≥ dτ/2 and Σ = {T = 0} is a Cauchy surface (it is even piecewise-smooth spacelike: 1 − 2∂_rτ − (∂_θτ/r)² ≥ 1 − 1/2 − 1/16 > 0). Every spear chart of a vertex on the axis is, on the spear, a rotation-translation (τ,z) ↦ (τ+a, e^{iα}z) (B21 prop:isom_strong), so its τ_Σ(z) = |Re(e^{iα}z)|/4 − a, not differentiable at z = 0. B21's proof (l.729) uses that Σ is smooth spacelike (transversality); with Σ smooth spacelike the statement is the printed one. Strongest true form for topological Σ, certified here: τ_Σ continuous on the closed disc (GX.E0Spear.continuousOn_tauS). gx's C¹ path (DEC-107/117) takes the C¹ rim circle from IsE0C1SpacelikeCauchy.rim (GXScaffold.BTZ.Surgery), not from Lemma 2.4.
questions: Lemma 2.4's 'smooth positive function τ_Σ': accept the C⁰ form (continuous on the closed disc, τ_Σ > v + R′/2) as the strongest true statement for B21's topological Cauchy surfaces (l.224), which would CLOSE the row (DEC-27)? Or should the counterexample Σ = {τ = |Re z|/4} ⊂ 𝔼₀ be formalized first (a separate package: Cauchy-ness of a kinked graph in 𝔼₀ plus the rigidity of spear charts; it is not a docstring edit), or a C¹ form be stated for a C¹ spacelike Σ (needs a notion of C¹ spacelike surface through the axis, which the strict library does not have)?
